title: Site-perfect models in a prescribed Tor interval
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and module-sheaf category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization and restriction to $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ be locally perfect: for every $U\in\mathcal C$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on which $E|_{U_i}$ is isomorphic to a bounded cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module sheaves, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers, and suppose the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] satisfy $H^r(E\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ for every $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $F$ in degree zero and every $r\notin[a,b]$. Then for every $U$ there is a covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ and bounded cochain complexes $P_j$ of $\mathcal O_{V_j}$-modules, with each $P_j^r$ a direct summand of a finite free module sheaf, such that $P_j^r=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ and $P_j\cong E|_{V_j}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{V_j})$.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), proof: the final displayed strictly perfect complex in degrees a through b; apply to a locally perfect E. Restriction of the Tor interval: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback). Upper-end shortening by local split surjections is explained also in the preceding pseudo-coherence section.

proof.text: Use the bounded flat representative supplied by the Tor interval to deduce vanishing of cohomology above b. Apply the local strict-perfect upper-model theorem to get charts with terms zero above b.

On each chart apply the lower-model theorem with a<=b and the original universal Tor interval. Its good lower truncation gives finite-free retract terms in [a,b]. Bind the covering sieves and apply transitivity to obtain the covering over the originally requested object.
